system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:28, Explorer wrote a UserAssist entry for ivy.chen whose ROT13-encoded path decodes to PowerShell at P:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe. This supports that PowerShell was recorded as used, but does not show its command line, purpose, or whether it was open at the reported 13:40 time.

At 13:39, WS-ICHEN-01 made a successful proxy CONNECT to download.windowsupdate.com using a Windows Update Agent user agent; the proxy record reports about 38.8 MB returned. This is consistent with update activity, but does not establish who initiated it or whether it was part of authorized patching.

At 13:38, the domain controller recorded a Kerberos service-ticket event for sam.okafor targeting WS-ICHEN-01, from source IP 10.40.10.23. This establishes ticket activity, not a completed interactive logon or the purpose of the access.
FILE-NWD-01 initiated a TCP connection to WS-ICHEN-01 on port 135 at 13:31; the connection record shows state S2. The available record does not establish what RPC operation, if any, occurred.
At 14:11 and 14:19, SYSTEM conhost.exe processes were created with csrss.exe as parent and then terminated. These records do not show that PowerShell was their child process or identify a command.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection for WS-ICHEN-01 was unavailable from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC, covering the reported time and the interval needed to establish process execution and logon details.
Network, DNS, and proxy sensors were reported as available, but the supplied records do not attribute the Windows Update transfer or the port 135 connection to a particular process or user.
The supplied records do not include a PowerShell process-creation event, command line, script-block log, or console contents for the reported window.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell was visibly open at approximately 13:40 UTC, and whether the 13:28 UserAssist entry corresponds to the reported window.
What command or script ran, its parent process, and whether it made changes or accessed sensitive data.
Whether the Kerberos ticket for sam.okafor resulted in a logon or was related to authorized patching.
What activity, if any, occurred over the FILE-NWD-01-to-WS-ICHEN-01 TCP port 135 connection.
Whether the observed activity was authorized, malicious, or unrelated to the reported PowerShell window.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain endpoint process, PowerShell, security, and EDR telemetry for WS-ICHEN-01 from 13:20 to 14:20 UTC, especially the 13:30–14:10 collection gap.
Collect PowerShell Operational logs, script-block or transcription logs, Prefetch and other execution artifacts, and available console or user-session evidence for the relevant period.
Identify the source host for 10.40.10.23 and obtain its activity plus domain-controller logon records to determine whether sam.okafor accessed WS-ICHEN-01.
Obtain RPC, SMB, and endpoint evidence for the 13:31 connection from FILE-NWD-01 to WS-ICHEN-01, and verify whether it corresponds to an authorized service or job.
Confirm with IT whether the 13:39 Windows Update transfer and any PowerShell use on ivy.chen's workstation were authorized patching or other planned work.
